requirements.requirement: Provide authoritative infra.test service with node1 as primary, node2 and node3 as secondaries, publishing app.infra.test as node1's service address and status.infra.test as TXT ready.
requirements.summary: Role-specific configurations were valid and all three authoritative services were active and enabled. Both secondaries served final serial 2026090106, app.infra.test as node1's 10.100.135.10 address, and status.infra.test as "ready".

requirements.requirement: Serve infra.test as a DNSSEC-signed zone.
requirements.summary: The final AXFR at serial 2026090106 passed cryptographic verification as fully signed with ECDSAP256SHA256, and both secondaries returned RRSIGs for the application record.

requirements.requirement: Configure node4 to resolve through both secondaries.
requirements.summary: Node4's active NetworkManager profile persistently lists node2 and node3 as its only DNS servers. Direct queries to each returned the required records and signatures, while default resolver and NSS lookups succeeded.

requirements.requirement: Support authenticated updates from node1 and propagate changes to both secondaries.
requirements.summary: A TSIG-authenticated update originating on node1 was accepted, signed, and observed on both secondaries at matching serial 2026090105. An unsigned update was refused. Authenticated cleanup advanced the serial to 2026090106 and propagated to both secondaries.

requirements.requirement: Keep node4 resolution available when one authoritative server is unavailable.
requirements.summary: Both secondaries first answered normally. Node2 was then stopped and confirmed to have no DNS listener; node4's direct query to it timed out while the default resolver automatically used node3 and returned app, status, DNSSEC signature, and NSS results. Node2 was restarted, answered correctly, and was subsequently observed synchronized at the final serial.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence, including DNSSEC verification, authenticated update propagation, and a complete healthy-baseline, node2-down failover, restoration, and recovered-state sequence. Only minor temporary-file residue detracts from operational hygiene.
limitations: The bounded disruption exercised loss of node2 only; the node1-down and node3-down permutations were not independently tested.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final lifecycle observations show no failed services or package-manager inconsistency, and the new DNS listeners are task-required and bound to the intended authoritative addresses. Minor executor-caused residue remains: bind installation logs and PID files on all nodes plus two AXFR verification files on node2 under /tmp.
